title: Tournament branch predictor combining local and global history
decision: Implement a tournament (hybrid) predictor that runs local-history and global-history predictors in parallel and dynamically selects between them with a choice predictor for each branch.
alternatives_or_rejected: Using only a local-history predictor or only a global-history predictor.
rationale: Different branches are better predicted by local versus global history; the choice predictor learns which is more accurate for each static branch, improving overall prediction accuracy beyond either predictor alone.
outcome: High prediction accuracy supporting aggressive speculative execution and the four-wide fetch pipeline.

title: Clustered integer execution units with cross-cluster bypass penalty
decision: Split the four integer units into two clusters, each with its own register-file copy; allow one-cycle penalty for results produced in one cluster and consumed in the other.
alternatives_or_rejected: A single fully-connected integer unit cluster with a multi-ported register file and full bypass network (would lengthen the critical execute-bypass path and cycle time).
rationale: Physical distance and the large number of register ports required for quad-issue made a monolithic organization incompatible with the target cycle time; simulations showed the cross-cluster penalty cost only about 1 % performance.
outcome: Maintained aggressive cycle time while still supporting four integer operations per cycle with acceptable IPC impact.

title: Out-of-order execution with large in-flight window
decision: Adopt a full out-of-order, register-renaming, speculative-execution core capable of holding many instructions in flight (on the order of 80) rather than remaining in-order like prior Alpha implementations.
alternatives_or_rejected: Continuing with a primarily in-order or limited out-of-order design as in the 21164.
rationale: Dynamic scheduling extracts more instruction-level parallelism and hides memory latency, necessary to keep the high-frequency pipeline fed and to reach the targeted SPECint/SPECfp numbers.
outcome: Sustained high IPC together with 500–600 MHz operation, delivering industry-leading benchmark scores.

title: Large on-chip L1 instruction and data caches (64 KB each)
decision: Increase L1 I- and D-caches to 64 KB each (versus the much smaller L1s of the 21164) and eliminate the need for an on-chip L2.
alternatives_or_rejected: Retaining smaller L1 caches plus an on-chip L2, or staying with the prior hierarchy sizes.
rationale: Larger L1s improve hit rates and reduce average memory latency for the out-of-order core; the external L2 interface was designed for very high bandwidth instead.
outcome: High L1 hit rates supporting the speculative core, together with an external L2 capable of multiple GB/s.

title: High-bandwidth external L2 and system interface prioritized over on-chip L2
decision: Provide a flexible, high-bandwidth interface to an off-chip L2 (and memory) that can sustain several GB/s rather than integrating a large on-chip L2.
alternatives_or_rejected: Spending die area on a large on-chip L2 at the expense of the external bandwidth or core resources.
rationale: Many important applications lack sufficient cache locality; raw bandwidth to external memory hierarchies is required for robust performance across the workload mix.
outcome: Sustained bandwidths reported in excess of 1 GB/s (user-visible) on streaming benchmarks and multi-GB/s peak to the L2.
